Subject: DPA questions: retention / deletion / backups (Caraway counterproposal attached)

Hi David,

Thanks for the draft DPA. Legal pushed back on a few retention points and asked that we raise them with you before redlining. Their main asks are:

- Clear timeline for deletion after termination (they want a firm number rather than 'commercially reasonable').
- Backup retention carveout: want assurance that onshore backup copies are not retained longer than the stated window and that backups are subject to the same erasure process.
- Proof-of-wipe: sample certificate or template they can reference in the DPA.

I attached Caraway's counterproposal (caraway-dpa-counterproposal.docx) with suggested wording. We also included a short list of required audit evidence items. Can you confirm what evidence Redwood can commit to and provide a proposed redline?

Also tagging Laura since she owns the evidence flow.

Hi Dana — thanks for the counterproposal and the clear asks. We're fine to continue in-thread and propose concrete language.

Quick answers up front:
- We can commit to a deletion trigger within a firm window post-termination and provide a certified wipe artifact (sample attached).
- Backups: we retain encrypted backups for disaster recovery; we can commit to a backup retention cap and a process to ensure backups are overwritten / expired within the agreed window.
- Evidence: we can provide an operational certificate of erasure and an audit log extract showing the deletion job execution (subject to redaction for multi-tenant metadata).

Laura — can you confirm the ops timeline below with Jonas and state if 45 days for certified erasure + 90 days for backup overwrite aligns with operational constraints? If not, what's the minimal safe window?

Dana — I sketched a candidate redline below that maps to our operational playbook. If anything in your counterproposal is non-starter please flag specific lines and we can iterate quickly.

Candidate language (summary):
"Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement, Redwood will, within thirty (30) days, delete Customer Content from active production systems. Redwood will provide a certificate of erasure within forty-five (45) days. Encrypted backups will be expired and overwritten within ninety (90) days from deletion trigger and will not be retained beyond that period, except to the extent required by law. Redwood will supply audit evidence that deletion and overwrite jobs executed, subject to reasonable redactions for platform multi-tenancy."

I attached a sample wipe certificate (sample-wipe-cert.txt) and a short ops runbook (erase-playbook.pdf).

Thanks —
David
Head of Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachments: sample-wipe-cert.txt, erase-playbook.pdf

Hi all — ops/infra here. Sorry for the longish note but wanted to be explicit about how this will work in our stack so legal can be confident the language maps to real steps.

Operational flow (high level):
1) Termination trigger: customer or Redwood triggers a termination job in the control plane. That sets the account to 'retire-pending'.
2) Active data deletion (0–30 days): we run account-scoped deletion across live object stores and indexes. This removes active records and associated model input payloads.
3) Tombstoning & replication (0–30 days): because of cross-region replication and eventual consistency, we tombstone items and remove primary references; tombstones are ephemeral and not queryable.
4) Backup expiry / overwrite (31–90 days): snapshot backups are scheduled for lifecycle deletion; backups are encrypted and kept for DR; we schedule overwrite tasks which zero-reference or rotate encryption keys depending on storage backend.
5) Certificate generation (by day 45): we capture job run IDs, task logs, and a hash-of-hashes artifact which we sign and hand to legal as the certificate of erasure. Sample attached.

Notes / constraints:
- Cold archival copies behind third-party archive providers may have vendor-imposed retention windows; for those we commit to instruct vendors to delete and request deletion receipts — but in rare cases vendor timelines can add latency.
- Instant purge vs. guaranteed overwrite: for some object stores we rely on TTL deletions which mark data for deletion and then garbage collection occurs; our guarantee is that customer data will not be accessible after the 30-day active deletion window and that backups will be invalidated within 90 days.
- Logs & telemetry: operational logs that contain customer identifiers are retained for incident response; we can provide audit extracts but will sanitize other tenants.

If Caraway wants stricter guarantees (e.g., immediate cryptographic key revocation that renders backups unreadable instantly) we can discuss adding a by-request key-revocation option — it has operational costs and will need to be scoped in Dedicated/Private deployments.

Let me know if you want me to translate any of this into explicit DPA boilerplate (I can produce a short appendix mapping each sentence to an ops artifact).

— Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

David / Jonas — thanks, that level of detail is helpful. A few follow-ups from legal:

1) Can you put the key timings numerically in the DPA (we prefer: 30/45/90 as you proposed).
2) For archival vendors, we need a fallback clause that says Redwood will "use commercially reasonable efforts" to obtain deletion receipts and will escalate to contractual remedies if receipts cannot be obtained within 60 days after the overwrite window.
3) Sample certificate format looks fine — can you confirm whether the signed hash-of-hashes includes the run IDs and timestamps? We need to map that to a playbook step so auditors can validate it.

If you can include the three items above in your next redline we can route this through Caraway procurement and legal. Also — we'll need a DocuSign link for the updated DPA once we have a working redline.

Best,
Dana

Dana — thanks, agreed. Below is the redline summary I'll put into the next DPA revision (we'll send a tracked copy via DocuSign link once Caraway confirms):

Proposed DPA language (to insert into Section X — Data Retention and Deletion):
1) Active Deletion: "Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Redwood will delete Customer Content from active production systems within thirty (30) days of the deletion trigger."
2) Certificate of Erasure: "Redwood will provide Customer a Certificate of Erasure within forty-five (45) days of the deletion trigger. The Certificate of Erasure will include job run identifiers, timestamps, and a signed hash-of-hashes sufficient to correlate the artifact with Redwood's internal deletion job logs, subject to reasonable redactions for multi-tenant metadata."
3) Backup Retention: "Encrypted backups and snapshots will be expired and overwritten within ninety (90) days of the deletion trigger. For third-party archival vendors, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain deletion receipts and will notify Customer of any vendor delays; if deletion receipts cannot be obtained within sixty (60) days after the overwrite window, Redwood will escalate per the remedies in Section Y."
4) Evidence: "Redwood will supply audit extracts and deletion job logs to Customer pursuant to a mutually agreed redaction and format; all evidence requests will be scoped to protect other customers' privacy and operational security."

Operational next steps:
- Jonas will provide an appendix mapping each DPA sentence to the corresponding ops artifact (job ID, log type, runbook step).
- I'll produce a tracked Word redline and generate a DocuSign envelope (link to follow).

Can we aim to have the tracked redline to you by 2028-03-04 EOD? That should keep the procurement timeline on track.

David Kim
Head of Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachments: erase-playbook.pdf (ops appendix), sample-wipe-cert.txt
